newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - March 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - March 14.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on March 14:
LOS ANGELES - An 18-year-old Russian emigre was being held in the roadside shooting death of Bill Cosby's son two months ago, an apparently random killing during a botched robbery attempt.
BAQURA, Jordan - A Jordanian military driver seized a comrade's M-16 rifle and opened fire at a group of Israeli schoolgirls touring this scenic border outpost, killing seven and wounding six.
WASHINGTON - A federal judge in Richmond has issued a broad order against race discrimination at Circuit City stores Inc., installing a court approved director of diversity management.
WASHINGTON - House Republican leaders, who with great fanfare set about to kill the National Endowment for the Arts two years ago, now say they don't have the votes to finish the job.

HOUSTON - In a federal court trial here, Mario Ruiz Massieu, a distinguished Mexican diplomat, author and attorney, is claiming that money -- asserted by prosecutors to be bribes from drug cartels -- came from family businesses and salary bonuses.
TIRANA, Albania - Albania tumbled into anarchy as the capital city resounded with gunfire, armed bandits roamed the countryside and panicked citizens stormed food warehouses and arms depots.
